lyrics:
I told a doctor, twenty years back
something wasn't right in me
She checked the numbers on the stack
and said, "That's just what age will be."

Maybe you're just getting older

No manual for growing old —
I filled the blank pages myself
called it tired, called it a cold
and put the question on a shelf

The decline got harder to deny
A year of pokes, and prods, and shocks
Test after test asked me why —
and none of them had stopped the clock

Not age. Not tired. Not a cold
Something I'd had since before the start
A man is a model, I'd been told —
turns out the model had a faulty part

My hands that gave out on a box I should have lifted
The race I dropped before the turn
The fence I couldn't clear
Not failure
A name I hadn't learned yet

Ring around the rosy
pocket full of posies
ashes, ashes
we all fall down

We all fall down
and somehow, it's still perfect
We all fall down —
not broken. Just built this way

We all fall down
and somehow, it's still perfect
We all fall down —
not broken. Just built this way

Ashes, ashes
We all fall down
Somehow, this too —
somehow, this too
lyrics_raw:
[Intro - flat, remembering]

[Verse 1 - plain, recalling]
I told a doctor, twenty years back,
something wasn't right in me.
She checked the numbers on the stack
and said, "That's just what age will be."

[Doctor - kind, dismissive]
Maybe you're just getting older.

[Verse 2 - resigned, self-taught]
No manual for growing old —
I filled the blank pages myself,
called it tired, called it a cold,
and put the question on a shelf.

[Interlude - years passing, unsettled]

[Verse 3 - clinical, wearing thin]
The decline got harder to deny.
A year of pokes, and prods, and shocks.
Test after test asked me why —
and none of them had stopped the clock.

[Verse 4 - quiet, arriving]
Not age. Not tired. Not a cold.
Something I'd had since before the start.
A man is a model, I'd been told —
turns out the model had a faulty part.

[Breakdown - quiet, connecting]
My hands that gave out on a box I should have lifted.
The race I dropped before the turn.
The fence I couldn't clear.

Not failure.
A name I hadn't learned yet.

[The Rhyme Returns - hushed, full circle]
Ring around the rosy,
pocket full of posies,
ashes, ashes,
we all fall down.

[Chorus - quiet, accepting]
We all fall down,
and somehow, it's still perfect.
We all fall down —
not broken. Just built this way.

[Interlude - warm, settling]

[Final Chorus - fuller, at peace]
We all fall down,
and somehow, it's still perfect.
We all fall down —
not broken. Just built this way.

[Outro - quiet, at peace]
Ashes, ashes.
We all fall down.
Somehow, this too —
somehow, this too.

[End]
style: Male baritone, resonant, plain clinical delivery warming into hushed acceptance, 70's Progressive rock, organ and piano in the verses, vibraphone entering for the nursery rhyme return, strings and warm electric piano for the chorus, Warm live-ensemble production, hushed and reverent, grace rather than grief

impression.text: This track establishes a melancholic yet theatrical emotional atmosphere, opening with an intimate piano and an emotive male vocal before expanding into a lush symphonic texture. The energy level builds steadily from a reflective ballad into a soaring stadium rock anthem, creating a passionate and dramatic feel. In terms of production, the mix is cinematic and wide, featuring a dense arrangement of electric guitars, sweeping strings, and heavy drums that sit perfectly balanced around the spacious lead vocal. A defining transition occurs when the sparse verses erupt into a massive and heavily orchestrated chorus, culminating later in a searing guitar solo before fading back into a delicate piano finish.

review.review_text: The trick here is the diagnosis reframed as a lyric: a doctor who checks "the numbers on the stack" and shrugs "maybe you're just getting older," and Rose turning twenty years of misfiling into a slow reveal. The line that pays it off, "turns out the model had a faulty part," lands because he's kept the delivery clinical up to that point, plain baritone over piano and organ, no reach for pity. Then the nursery rhyme returns, "ring around the rosy" flipped from playground doom into acceptance, and the chorus arrives at "not broken. Just built this way," which is the whole record's argument in six words. It runs 4:08 in C major at a brisk 136, and the build from hushed verse to full-ensemble chorus is more stadium than the material strictly needs; the guitar solo late is the one place grace tips toward grandeur. Reminds me of Warren Zevon staring down his own body without blinking. A highlight, and it holds the room.
